proposal: The Mandate recommends that DOL and the NLRB return to their 2019 and 2021 independent contractor rules and to a joint employer test based on direct and immediate control. It also asks Congress for a bright-line control test across federal laws, a benefits safe harbor for independent workers, and the Save Local Business Act.

status_summary: DOL stopped applying the 2024 independent contractor rule in its investigations on 2025-05-01. On 2026-02-27 DOL proposed replacing that rule with the 2021 framework (with modifications), and on 2026-04-23 it proposed restoring a joint employer rule under the FLSA, FMLA and MSPA; comment periods closed 2026-04-28 and 2026-06-22 and no final rules were found as of 2026-10-07. The NLRB on 2026-02-27 published a final rule restoring the 2020 joint employer text (direct and immediate control); because a court had vacated the 2023 rule in March 2024 before it took effect, the 2020 standard was already the one in use, and the 2026 rule formally restored its text. The NLRB's independent contractor standard was not checked.

timeline.event: DOL's Wage and Hour Division issues Field Assistance Bulletin 2025-1 (Acting Administrator Donald M. Harrison III): from this date WHD no longer applies the 2024 independent contractor rule's analysis in FLSA investigations and relies on Fact Sheet #13 (2008) as informed by Opinion Letter FLSA2019-6; the 2024 rule remains in effect for private litigation.

DOL publishes a proposed rule to rescind the 2024 independent contractor analysis and restore the January 2021 analysis, with changes, for the FLSA, FMLA and MSPA. Comments closed 2026-04-28 with 16,522 received. Five lawsuits against the 2024 rule remain stayed pending reconsideration.

NLRB publishes a final rule, effective immediately and issued without notice and comment, that replaces the vacated 2023 joint employer rule text with the 2020 rule, which requires substantial direct and immediate control over essential terms of employment. The 2023 rule had been vacated by a federal court in Texas in March 2024.

DOL publishes a proposed rule restoring joint employer regulations under the FLSA (29 CFR part 791) and tying FMLA and MSPA rules to it; the test looks at hiring and firing, supervision of schedules or conditions, pay, and records, and states that franchising alone does not determine joint employer status. Comments closed 2026-06-22 with 263 received.

title: Return to 2021 independent contractor and direct-control joint employer standards
uncertainties: The NLRB's independent contractor standard (Board adjudication) was not checked. Federal Register queries on 2026-10-13 (Wage and Hour Division rules after 2026-04-24, and Labor Department documents mentioning independent contractor after 2026-04-24) found no final independent contractor or joint employer rule; the Wage and Hour rules listed were a coordinated enforcement rescission (2026-08-31), penalty inflation adjustments and an overtime exemption rule implementing court judgments (2026-05-15), none on these topics. A final rule could still be at OIRA review without appearing there. One web search returned only law firm summaries of the February to April 2026 actions and a Wage and Hour regulatory agenda article (not opened); no litigation over these rules was found. Congressional bills were not searched.
